questions.question:

questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Swallows build new nests every year.

options.text: New nests were built by swallows every year
New nests are built by swallows every year.
New nests were being built by swallows every year.
New nests is being built by swallows every year.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In English, passive sentences are formed by rearranging the subject, the verb, and the object of the sentence.
 
• The **object **of the active sentence** becomes** the **subject** of the passive sentence.
 
• **The verb** in the passive sentence is formed by using the appropriate form of **"to be" **plus the past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this case,** "build" **is the main verb, and its past participle is **"built."**
 
• **In the sentence** "Swallows build new nests every year", the **present simple tense **is used, which suggests a repeated or regular action.
 
• When converted into the passive voice, the same tense (present simple) should be maintained.
 
• Therefore, the **appropriate form of "to be" is "are".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: '*New nests are built by swallows every year'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the other options:
 
 
• **New nests were built by swallows every year** - This uses the past simple tense ("were built"), so it is not the correct conversion from the original sentence, which is in the present simple tense.
 
• **New nests were being built by swallows every year** - This uses the past continuous tense ("were being built"), so it is not the correct conversion from the original sentence, which is in the present simple tense.
 
• **New nests is being built by swallows every year **- This is incorrect grammatically. "Is being built" is present continuous tense and used for ongoing actions, and the subject "new nests" is plural, which should take "are" instead of "is".

questions.question:
Choose the option that is the correct direct form of the sentence.

The teacher asked me if I had seen the match.

options.text: "Did you see the match?" the teacher said to me.
"Did you had saw the match?" the teacher said to me.
"Did you saw the match?" the teacher said to me.
"Did you seen the match?" the teacher said to me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In reported or indirect speech, the **present simple tense** in direct speech **changes to** the **past simple**.
 
• Similarly, the **past simple tense **in direct speech **changes **to the **past perfect.**
 
• Therefore, when** we convert the indirect speech back to direct**, we **revert** this change.
 
• In the sentence "The teacher asked me if I had seen the match", the phrase **"had seen"** is in the **past perfect tense.**
 
• In direct speech, this would have been in the past simple tense, which is **"did see" **or more commonly expressed as** "did you see".**

Therefore, the **correct direct form **of the sentence: *"The teacher asked me if I had seen the match" is "Did you see the match?" the teacher said to me.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Now, let's analyze the incorrect options:
 
 
• **"Did you had saw the match?" the teacher said to me.-** This sentence is grammatically incorrect. We **don't use "did" with "had"** or the past participle "saw".
 
• **"Did you saw the match?" the teacher said to me. - **This sentence is also grammatically incorrect. **After "did", we use the base form **of the verb, which is "see", not the past form "saw".
 
• **"Did you seen the match?" the teacher said to me. -** This sentence is grammatically incorrect. **After "did", we use the base form** of the verb, which is "see", not the past participle "seen".
